questions.enonce_markdown: List any three (3) factors that affect the rate of this reaction. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Any three of:

1. **Concentration** of the hydrochloric acid.
2. **Temperature** of the reaction mixture.
3. **Surface area** (particle size) of the calcium carbonate: lumps or powder.

questions.enonce_markdown: Describe the effect of change of each of the factors on the reaction rate. *[15 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**1. Concentration of the acid.** Increasing the concentration of HCl **increases** the rate. There are more acid particles in the same volume, so the particles collide **more often** with the calcium carbonate and more successful collisions occur each second. Using more dilute acid slows the reaction down (the graph of volume of gas against time is less steep).

**2. Temperature.** Increasing the temperature **increases** the rate. The particles move faster and have more kinetic energy, so they collide more often and, above all, a **larger fraction of collisions has energy equal to or greater than the activation energy**. A rise of about $10^\circ$C roughly doubles the rate. Lower temperature gives a slower reaction.

**3. Surface area (particle size) of calcium carbonate.** Crushing the lumps into a powder **increases** the rate. Smaller pieces expose a **larger surface area** to the acid, so more particles of the solid can collide with acid particles at the same time. Large lumps react slowly because only the outside surface is in contact with the acid.

*Note:* in every case the **total volume of carbon dioxide** finally obtained is the same (it depends only on the quantity of the limiting reactant); only the **speed** at which it is produced changes.

questions.enonce_markdown: Name the equipment that can be used to record the volume of carbon dioxide evolved over an interval of time. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: A **gas syringe** connected to the reaction flask (the volume of gas is read from the syringe at regular time intervals with a **stopwatch**). Alternatively, the gas can be collected over water in an inverted measuring cylinder or burette.
